title: Mekatilili wa Menza
summary: A Giriama woman from present-day Kilifi County, Mekatilili wa Menza spoke at meetings at the Kaya Fungo shrine in July and August 1913, where anti-British oaths were sworn, and confronted an administrator at a baraza at Chakama on 13 August 1913. She was arrested on 17 October 1913, held in Kisii, was back in the Kaya after 1919 and died in 1924. The pin marks Chakama.

uncertainty.note: Birth is given as the 1840s or 1860s; death year is 1924 in both sources (some sources say 1925).

as_recorded.value: In July and August 1913 she spoke at meetings at the kaya fungo

where.modern_name: Chakama, Magarini, Kilifi County, Kenya (pinned to the site of the 13 August 1913 baraza; Kaya Fungo, Giriama country, has no confirmed coordinates)
where.historical_name: Chakama, Giriama country, East Africa Protectorate (British colonial rule)

importance.justification: Led Giriama resistance to British colonial labour and recruitment demands in 1913.

sources.title: Mekatilili Wa Menza And The Giriama War
Mekatilili wa Menza: Giriama Freedom Fighter Against Colonial Rule

reviewer_note: Sources differ: Sheffield says she was recaptured two days after returning home (January 1914); Kenyanhistory.com says rearrested in August 1914 and held at Kismayu. Chakama is named only by Kenyanhistory.com. OSM point for Chakama; Kaya Fungo location not found.
